findings.title: Scope the retry-count purge to SMS reminders
Guard the retry-count update inside the catch block
Use an atomic increment instead of read-modify-write
Unindexed `retryCount` predicate in an `OR` delete on every cron run
Reminders are silently dropped after retries are exhausted

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Scope the retry-count purge to SMS reminders

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29-45

Explanation:
The second `OR` branch (`retryCount > 1`) does not filter on `method`. This SMS cron job will therefore delete any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, whatever its method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, …).

`retryCount` is a general column on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table. If any other scheduler starts incrementing it (or already does), this job will silently delete that scheduler's reminders.

The branch also ignores `scheduled` state. It could remove reminders that were later scheduled successfully, along with their `referenceId`, which breaks later cancellation of the provider-side message.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({
  where: {
    method: WorkflowMethods.SMS,
    OR: [
      { scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } },
      { retryCount: { gt: 1 }, scheduled: false },
    ],
  },
});
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Reliability
Title: Guard the retry-count update inside the catch block

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189-198

Explanation:
`prisma.workflowReminder.update` is now awaited inside the `catch`. If that update throws, the exception escapes the per-reminder try/catch. Possible causes include:
- a transient DB error (the original failure may itself have been DB-related),
- the record being deleted concurrently, which gives `RecordNotFound`.

When that happens, the whole loop is aborted, every remaining reminder is skipped for this run, and the handler ends with an unhandled error. Before this change, a single failure was only logged and processing continued.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
} catch (error) {
  console.log(`Error scheduling SMS with error ${error}`);
  try {
    await prisma.workflowReminder.update({
      where: { id: reminder.id },
      data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
    });
  } catch (updateError) {
    console.log(`Failed to increment retryCount for reminder ${reminder.id}: ${updateError}`);
  }
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Use an atomic increment instead of read-modify-write

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:179-186
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190-197

Explanation:
The code writes `reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at the start of the job. If cron invocations overlap, or the same reminder is processed twice, increments get lost. A failing reminder could then be retried more times than intended.

Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` is atomic and also removes the need for the extra `select`/cast.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } },
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Unindexed `retryCount` predicate in an `OR` delete on every cron run

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:31-43
- packages/prisma/schema.prisma:1000

Explanation:
`OR` with an unindexed `retryCount > 1` predicate prevents the planner from using only the existing indexes. The result is likely a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table on every cron invocation, and that table grows with every booking.

Fix options:
- Scope the delete by `method` and `scheduled` (see issue 1).
- Run the retry purge as a separate, narrower `deleteMany`.
- Add an index, e.g. `@@index([method, retryCount])`, if the query stays.

Proposed fix:
~~~prisma
@@index([method, scheduled, retryCount])
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Reminders are silently dropped after retries are exhausted

Affected:
- packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38-42

Explanation:
After two failed attempts, the reminder row is simply deleted on the next run. Nothing is logged and nothing marks it as failed, so the attendee never gets the SMS and there is no trace of why.

The threshold `1` is also a magic number, and with `gt: 1` the reminder gets only 2 attempts, which may not match the intent.

The fix: extract a named constant such as `MAX_SMS_RETRIES`, and log or flag reminders before purging them.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const MAX_SMS_RETRY_COUNT = 2;
// ...
{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduled: false, retryCount: { gte: MAX_SMS_RETRY_COUNT } }
~~~
